records.our_prose: Broccoli microgreens are the young seedlings of broccoli (Brassica oleracea var. italica), harvested at the cotyledon to first-true-leaf stage about 8 to 12 days after sowing. They are grown indoors year-round in a short repeatable cycle: a dense, dry, even sow on a shallow tray of mix or a fiber mat (broccoli needs no presoak), a brief dark blackout of about 3 to 4 days to drive even germination and stem stretch, then light to green up, then a single cut. The flavor is mild, fresh, and faintly cabbage-like. Broccoli is one of the most popular microgreens for nutrition; like other brassica microgreens it concentrates the glucosinolates that give the cabbage family its character, and research finds microgreens generally higher in vitamins and phytochemicals than the mature vegetable. Because there is no frost, season, or hardiness zone involved, the same tray grows identically on a windowsill anywhere.

records.our_prose: Soil-borne fungi and water molds (Pythium, Rhizoctonia, and Fusarium) rot seedlings at the base under wet, crowded, still conditions, often alongside fuzzy white cobweb-like growth on the medium and stems. Broccoli is a small, densely sown brassica and is notably prone to it; on Penn State's trials damping-off was the only disease or pest issue encountered.

records.our_prose: Sow densely and evenly across pre-moistened medium (about 28 grams, roughly 1 ounce, of broccoli seed per 1020 tray; small-seeded brassicas can go as dense as about 10 to 12 seeds per square inch). Broccoli takes no presoak; the seed goes on dry. Do not bury it; press it into firm contact, then cover for a dark blackout period. Dense, even contact is what gives a uniform stand and a clean single cut.
records.source_context: As a general rule, the optimal seed density ranges from 2 seeds per square inch for larger seeds up to 12 seeds per square inch for the smaller seeds (from 1 to 6 seeds per cm 2 if you prefer the metric system).

records.our_prose: For a mild, versatile tray, standard broccoli (Brassica oleracea var. italica) is the mainstay: small brassica seed sown densely and dry (no presoak), finishing in about 8 to 12 days. Broccoli is one of the microgreens most often grown for nutrition; like other brassica microgreens it concentrates the glucosinolates that give the cabbage family its character, and research finds microgreens generally higher in vitamins and phytochemicals than the mature vegetable. For a sharper tray, broccoli raab (rapini) is a peppery alternative, but note it is a different species (Brassica rapa, closer to turnip) rather than true broccoli. Never grow microgreens from solanaceous seed (tomato, pepper, eggplant); those seedlings are not safe to eat raw.
